slides.title: Disjoint Sets and Backtracking
slides.main: In both cases the main job is not to do extra work.

captions: Disjoint sets: remember who is merged with whom
Backtracking: walk the options and prune hopeless branches
In both cases the job is to avoid extra work

slides.title: Dynamic connectivity
slides.main: union merges groups, find tells whether two elements share a group.

captions: At first every element is its own group
union(0, 1), union(1, 2) and union(3, 4): two bigger groups appear
union(2, 3) merged them into one group of five
find(0) == find(4)? Yes: same group, while 5, 6 and 7 are still alone

slides.title: A forest in an array
slides.sub: Everyone has a parent, the root is the representative
slides.main: A root has parent[x] = x; a union is a single assignment.

captions: Each element has a parent; a root is its own parent and represents the group
find(1): climb 1 → 0, root found
union(0, 3): hang root 3 under root 0 with one assignment
The naive version can stretch into a chain, making find linear

slides.title: Path compression
slides.main: After find, every element on the path points straight to the root.

captions: A chain of five: each points to the previous one
find(4): walk 4 → 3 → 2 → 1 → 0 and find the root
On the way back, re-hang everyone straight onto the root
Now find(4) is one step; the tree is almost flat

slides.title: Union by size
slides.main: Height at most log₂ n; with compression, nearly constant.

captions: Roots of two trees: sizes 4 and 2
Larger under smaller: height grows to 3
Smaller under larger: height stays 2
Always hang the smaller under the larger: height at most log₂ n

slides.title: Where it is used
slides.main: If groups only merge and never split, think disjoint sets.

captions: Count components and catch a cycle: an edge inside a group closes one
Kruskal: edges by increasing weight, take those joining different groups
Islands and equalities: anything that only merges and never splits

slides.title: Data in the root
slides.main: The root stores group info; with edge weights, the distance to the root.

captions: The root stores group info: size, sum, minimum
On union they are combined: one node speaks for the whole group
With weights on parent edges we tell how much one element exceeds another

frames.text: two groups with their own data

slides.title: Brute force and the option tree
slides.main: Brute force is the universal way to a correct answer when nothing better exists.

captions: Each step has several ways to continue: take it or not
All options form a tree; as many leaves as answers
A root-to-leaf path is one option: for example, the subset {a, c}
Subsets: 2ⁿ, permutations: n!: at n = 20 that is millions and quintillions

slides.title: The backtracking template
slides.main: Mutate one shared list in place and always undo the choice.

captions: The recursion receives a partial answer path
If the answer is complete, record it and return
Otherwise: choose an option, go deeper, undo the choice
Don't forget the copy: otherwise all answers share one mutable list

slides.title: Pruning
slides.main: As soon as a partial answer is hopeless, cut the branch.

captions: Place one queen per row; no queen may attack another
A corner queen blocks a column and a diagonal: gray cells are forbidden
Place the second-row queen on an allowed cell
Row three is fully attacked: backtrack and try another cell above

slides.title: Subsets, permutations, combinations
slides.main: Duplicates: sort, then skip equal neighbors on the same level.

captions: Two options per element: take it or not
At each step pick any element not yet used
Take elements in increasing index order — order doesn't matter
Sort the input and skip an element equal to the previous one on this level

slides.title: Sum with pruning
slides.main: If a number exceeds the remainder, try nothing further; masks and meet-in-the-middle for small n.

captions: Target 7; numbers 2, 3, 6, 7 sorted; each node shows the remainder
Take any number: 7 gives zero and success, 6 leaves 1 — hopeless
From five take 2 or 3; from four only 3; path 2 + 2 + 3 = 7 is done
If a number exceeds the remainder, all later ones do too — break the loop

slides.title: Summary
slides.main: A parent array with compression and size; “choose, explore, undo” with pruning.

captions: Disjoint sets — a forest in one array
Compression and size give nearly constant time per operation
Backtracking gives the search, pruning gives its speed
